exactly as they are: OnWrite and OnDelete.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentExists
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentExists: Insert over a taken key.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentKeyChanged
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentKeyChanged: an Update's function changed the key.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentKeyEmpty
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentKeyEmpty: the key function returned the empty string.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentNotFound
symbols.doc:
CodeDocumentNotFound: no document under the key, or nobody holds the
key in a unique index.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentNotTrashed
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentNotTrashed: no document is in the trash under the key.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentUndecodable
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentUndecodable: a stored document no longer fits the type.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentUnencodable
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentUnencodable: encoding/json refused the value.

symbols.name: CodeIndexBroken
symbols.doc: CodeIndexBroken: the stored documents break a unique index.

symbols.name: CodeIndexNotUnique
symbols.doc: CodeIndexNotUnique: Lookup on a multi-valued index.

symbols.name: CodeIndexUnknown
symbols.doc: CodeIndexUnknown: a read named an index the store never declared.

symbols.name: CodeKeyTooLong
symbols.doc: CodeKeyTooLong: a key is longer than the SQL store's key columns hold.

symbols.name: CodeLoadFailed
symbols.doc: CodeLoadFailed: the store's files cannot be read or are not a store's.

symbols.name: CodePersistFailed
symbols.doc: CodePersistFailed: the filesystem refused the write; nothing changed.

symbols.name: CodeStatementFailed
symbols.doc: CodeStatementFailed: the SQL store's database did not complete a call.

symbols.name: CodeStoreClosed
symbols.doc: CodeStoreClosed: a call after Close.

symbols.name: CodeStoreMisconfigured
symbols.doc: CodeStoreMisconfigured: Open refused its configuration.

symbols.name: CodeUniqueKeyTaken
symbols.doc: CodeUniqueKeyTaken: a unique index refused the write.

symbols.name: CodeVersionNotFound
symbols.doc: CodeVersionNotFound: the document keeps no version of that number.

symbols.name: CodeVersionsInvalid
symbols.doc: CodeVersionsInvalid: versions PutDocument cannot write as they are given.

symbols.name: CodeVersionsNotKept
symbols.doc: CodeVersionsNotKept: a call on versions to a store that keeps none.

symbols.name: CodeVersionsRewriteRefused
symbols.doc: CodeVersionsRewriteRefused: a rewrite returned what a rewrite may not.

symbols.name: CodeWriteUnconfirmed
symbols.doc: CodeWriteUnconfirmed: the write stands, its durability is in doubt.

symbols.name: Collection
symbols.doc:
Collection is the public alias for the port of a store whose calls take no
context, which [Store] implements: Get, List, Filter, Entries, Lookup and
Find; Put, Insert, Replace, Update and Delete; OnWrite and OnDelete. It is
what a caller depends on to stand a double in for a [Store]; Stats, Fold
and Close are the engine's own.

symbols.name: CollectionContext
symbols.doc:
CollectionContext is the public alias for [Collection] with a context on
every call, which [SQLStore] implements; Count and Reindex are the engine's
own.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config is the public alias for a store's configuration: Key (required), FS
and Path (both, or neither for a memory store), FoldAt, and Versions with
its Clock and Held.

symbols.name: DefaultFoldAt
symbols.doc:
DefaultFoldAt is the least number of overlay entries that folds the overlay
into the snapshot when [Config].FoldAt is zero.

symbols.name: DocumentExists

code.public: A document already has this key

symbols.doc: DocumentExists refuses an insertion over a taken key.

symbols.name: DocumentKeyChanged

code.public: An update cannot change a document's key

symbols.doc: DocumentKeyChanged refuses an update that renames.

symbols.name: DocumentKeyEmpty

code.public: A document's key cannot be empty

symbols.doc: DocumentKeyEmpty refuses a document whose key is empty.

symbols.name: DocumentNotFound

code.public: No document has this key

symbols.doc: DocumentNotFound is a miss.

symbols.name: DocumentNotTrashed

code.public: No document with this key is in the trash

symbols.doc: DocumentNotTrashed is a miss on the trash: no document is trashed under the key.

symbols.name: DocumentUndecodable

code.public: A stored document does not match its type

symbols.doc: DocumentUndecodable reports a stored document the type no longer fits.

symbols.name: DocumentUnencodable

code.public: The document cannot be encoded

symbols.doc: DocumentUnencodable refuses a value encoding/json cannot encode.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc: Entry is the public alias for one stored document as JSON, with its key.

symbols.name: Index
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, keys func(T) []string) IndexSpec[T]
symbols.doc:
Index declares an index where a document may have several keys and a key
several documents. Empty keys are not indexed.

symbols.name: IndexBroken

code.public: The stored documents break a unique index

symbols.doc: IndexBroken refuses documents that break a unique index.

symbols.name: IndexNotUnique

code.public: The index is not unique: read it with Find

symbols.doc: IndexNotUnique refuses a Lookup on a multi-valued index.

symbols.name: IndexSpec
symbols.doc:
IndexSpec is the public alias for one secondary index's declaration, built
by [Unique] or [Index] and given to [Open].

symbols.name: IndexUnknown

code.public: The store has no index of this name

symbols.doc: IndexUnknown refuses a read of an undeclared index.

symbols.name: KeyLister
symbols.doc:
KeyLister is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection] that lists
the documents' keys alone, in key order and without a context, which
[Store] implements: Keys.

symbols.name: KeyListerContext
symbols.doc:
KeyListerContext is the public alias for [KeyLister] with a context on
every call, which [SQLStore] implements.

symbols.name: KeyTooLong

code.public: A key is longer than the store can keep

symbols.doc: KeyTooLong refuses a key longer than the SQL store's key columns hold.

symbols.name: LoadFailed

code.public: The store's files could not be loaded

symbols.doc: LoadFailed refuses files that are not a store's.

symbols.name: MaxSQLIndexNameLen
symbols.doc: MaxSQLIndexNameLen is the longest index name a SQL store accepts, in bytes.

symbols.name: MaxSQLKeyLen
symbols.doc:
MaxSQLKeyLen is the longest store key, and the longest index key as it
reaches the table, a SQL store accepts, in bytes.

symbols.name: MaxSQLTableLen
symbols.doc:
MaxSQLTableLen is the longest table name [OpenSQL] and [SQLMigration]
accept, in bytes: PostgreSQL's limit of 63, less what the store appends to
derive its index table's name.

symbols.name: Open
symbols.doc:
Open builds a store from cfg with the secondary indexes given: in memory
without a filesystem, otherwise loaded from it — the snapshot, the overlay
replayed on top, the indexes rebuilt. It creates the directories the store
lives in, 0700, and writes its files 0600.

symbols.name: OpenSQL
symbols.doc:
OpenSQL builds a store over SQL from cfg with the secondary indexes given,
declared as for [Open]. It sends no statement: its tables are
[SQLMigration]'s, run by the caller's Migrator before the store is used.

symbols.name: PersistFailed

code.public: The document could not be written to storage

symbols.doc: PersistFailed reports a write the filesystem refused.

symbols.name: SQLConfig
symbols.doc:
SQLConfig is the public alias for a SQL store's configuration: Key,
Transactor, Dialect and Table (required), IndexKey, and Versions with its
Clock and Held.

symbols.name: SQLMigration
symbols.spelled: func(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
symbols.canonical: func(dialect github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Migration, error)
symbols.doc:
SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the two tables a SQL store
named table keeps on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version
table. Its Down drops both, and every document in them. Every statement does
nothing when its table exists, so a run MySQL's implicit commit stopped
halfway completes when it runs again.

symbols.name: SQLStore
symbols.doc:
SQLStore is the public alias for the document store over SQL: Get, List,
Filter, Entries, Keys, Count, Lookup and Find read; Put, Insert, Replace, Update
and Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make
records; Versions, Version and RewriteVersions, Trash, Restore, Purge and
Tombstones as for [Store]; OnWrite and OnDelete announce once the write's
transaction commits; Reindex files the stored documents again. Every call
takes a context.

symbols.name: SQLVersionsMigration
symbols.spelled: func(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
symbols.canonical: func(dialect github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Migration, error)
symbols.doc:
SQLVersionsMigration returns the migration that creates the table a SQL
store named table keeps its versions in on dialect, numbered version for the
caller's own version table, beside [SQLMigration]'s. A store opened with
[SQLConfig].Versions needs it. Its Down drops the table, and every version
in it: run it to turn versions off for good.

symbols.name: Stamp
symbols.doc:
Stamp is the public alias for what a Stamped write says about the version
it makes: the Meta the version records, or InPlace — no version.

symbols.name: StatementFailed

code.public: The store's database did not complete the request

symbols.doc:
StatementFailed reports a call the SQL store's database did not
complete; the driver's error is joined beside it, its text withheld.

symbols.name: Stats
symbols.doc:
Stats is the public alias for what a store says about itself: documents,
pending overlay entries, folds, and the last automatic fold's failure.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the public alias for the document store: Get, List, Filter,
Entries, Keys, Lookup, Find and Stats read; Put, Insert, Replace, Update and
Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make
records; Versions and Version read a document's versions, RewriteVersions
rewrites its former ones; Trash, Restore, Purge and Tombstones keep its
trash; OnWrite and OnDelete announce; Fold and Close bring it to rest.

symbols.name: StoreClosed

code.public: The store is closed

symbols.doc: StoreClosed refuses a call after Close.

symbols.name: StoreMisconfigured

code.public: The document store cannot be opened as configured

symbols.doc: StoreMisconfigured refuses a configuration no store could honour.

symbols.name: Tombstone
symbols.doc:
Tombstone is the public alias for a document in the trash, as Tombstones
lists it: its Key, and the instant At it was trashed.

symbols.name: Trashable
symbols.doc:
Trashable is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection] that keeps a
document's trash without a context, which [Store] implements: Trash,
Restore, Purge and Tombstones.

symbols.name: TrashableContext
symbols.doc:
TrashableContext is the public alias for [Trashable] with a context on
every call, which [SQLStore] implements.

symbols.name: Unique
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string) IndexSpec[T]
symbols.canonical: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/docstore.IndexSpec[T]
symbols.doc:
Unique declares a unique index over the one key key returns. An empty key is
not indexed, so any number of documents may have none.

symbols.name: UniqueKeyTaken

code.public: Another document already has this key in a unique index

symbols.doc: UniqueKeyTaken refuses a write a unique index cannot file.

symbols.name: Version
symbols.doc:
Version is the public alias for one version of a document: its Number from
1, the instant At the write that made it ran, the Meta that write carried,
and the document as JSON.

symbols.name: VersionNotFound

code.public: The document keeps no version of this number

symbols.doc: VersionNotFound is a miss on a version: never made, or pruned.

symbols.name: VersionWriter
symbols.doc:
VersionWriter is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection] that
writes a document with its versions — numbers, instants, metadata — and
its trash as they are given, which [Store] implements: PutDocument. A
copy from one engine to another needs it.

symbols.name: VersionWriterContext
symbols.doc:
VersionWriterContext is the public alias for [VersionWriter] with a
context on every call, which [SQLStore] implements.

symbols.name: Versioned
symbols.doc:
Versioned is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection] that reads and
writes a document's versions without a context, which [Store] implements:
the four Stamped writes, Versions, Version and RewriteVersions.

symbols.name: VersionedContext
symbols.doc:
VersionedContext is the public alias for [Versioned] with a context on every
call, which [SQLStore] implements beside [CollectionContext].

symbols.name: VersionsInvalid

code.public: The document's versions cannot be written as they were given

symbols.doc: VersionsInvalid refuses versions PutDocument cannot write as they are given.

symbols.name: VersionsNotKept

code.public: This store keeps no versions

symbols.doc: VersionsNotKept refuses a call on versions to a store that keeps none.

symbols.name: VersionsRewriteRefused

code.public: A rewrite of versions may only drop or rewrite the versions it was given

symbols.doc: VersionsRewriteRefused refuses what a rewrite's function returned.

symbols.name: WriteUnconfirmed

code.public: The document was stored, but its durability could not be confirmed

symbols.doc:
WriteUnconfirmed reports a write that stands but may not survive a
power loss.

symbols.name: Broker
symbols.doc:
Broker is the public alias for the queue contract. It is FROZEN at four
methods; capabilities arrive as siblings ([DeadLetterReader],
[LeaseExtender], [Waker], [Rejecter], [DeadLetterManager]) reached by type
assertion.

symbols.name: CodeDeadLetterNotFound
symbols.doc: CodeDeadLetterNotFound is [DeadLetterNotFound]'s code.

symbols.name: CodeNotRetryable
symbols.doc:
CodeNotRetryable is the code [DoNotRetry] adds to a failure's wrap
trail: errs.HasCode(err, CodeNotRetryable) recognises the mark, where
errors.Is(err, NotRetryable) sees only an origin.

symbols.name: CodeSQLQueueMisconfigured
symbols.doc: CodeSQLQueueMisconfigured is [SQLQueueMisconfigured]'s code.

symbols.name: Consume
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, broker Broker, cfg ConsumerConfig) error
symbols.doc:
Consume runs cfg.Handler against broker until ctx is done, on
cfg.Parallelism goroutines it owns.

It returns nil when ctx ends — a cancelled consumer is a stopped consumer,
not a failed one — and returns the broker's error when the STORAGE fails. A
handler's error is never returned: it is nacked, retried, and eventually
dead-lettered, which is the entire point of the domain.

cfg.HandlerIsIdempotent must be true; see the package documentation.

symbols.name: ConsumerConfig
symbols.doc: ConsumerConfig is the public alias for [Consume]'s configuration.

symbols.name: ConsumerMisconfigured

code.public: The consumer configuration is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
ConsumerMisconfigured refuses a consumer with no Handler, or one whose
author has not asserted HandlerIsIdempotent.

symbols.name: DeadLetter
symbols.doc: DeadLetter is the public alias for one abandoned message and its cause.

symbols.name: DeadLetterManager
symbols.doc:
DeadLetterManager is the public alias for the capability of replaying a
dead letter into its queue, its count reset, or deleting it. Every broker
here implements it.

symbols.name: DeadLetterNotFound

code.public: No dead letter has that identifier

symbols.doc:
DeadLetterNotFound refuses a replay or a deletion naming a dead letter
the store does not hold.

symbols.name: DeadLetterReader
symbols.doc:
DeadLetterReader is the public alias for the capability of reading the
dead-letter store back. Every broker here implements it.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxMessageBytes
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxMessageBytes is the payload bound applied when
[Policy].MaxMessageBytes is left at zero: one mebibyte.

symbols.name: DefaultPollInterval
symbols.doc:
DefaultPollInterval is how long an idle worker waits before asking again
when [ConsumerConfig].PollInterval is left at zero. With a [Waker] broker it
bounds only how late another process's publication is noticed.

symbols.name: Delivery
symbols.doc:
Delivery is the public alias for one message handed to one consumer,
carrying the lease that proves the claim and the count that says whether
this is a retry.

symbols.name: DoNotRetry
symbols.doc:
DoNotRetry marks cause as a failure no retry can fix: returned from a
[Handler], it makes [Consume] dead-letter the message at once, with cause,
instead of handing it back for another attempt. An SDK error keeps its own
reason, code and public words in the dead letter; any other error, or none,
is recorded as [NotRetryable].

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc: FileConfig is the public alias for [NewFile]'s configuration.

symbols.name: Handler
symbols.doc: Handler is the public alias for the function that processes one delivery.

symbols.name: HandlerPanicked

code.public: The queue handler panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
HandlerPanicked reports a recovered handler panic. The message was
nacked and the consumer kept running.

There is deliberately no HandlerFailed beside it: a handler that
returns an error has its error recorded in the dead letter unmodified,
because a verdict wrapped around it would displace the reason whoever
reads that record actually needs.

symbols.name: InvalidBatchSize

code.public: A batch size must be positive

symbols.doc: InvalidBatchSize refuses a non-positive batch size.

symbols.name: Lease
symbols.doc: Lease is the public alias for a consumer's exclusive claim on one message.

symbols.name: LeaseExpired

code.public: The lease on that message has expired and the acknowledgement was ignored

symbols.doc:
LeaseExpired reports an acknowledgement whose lease had already lapsed.
Nothing happened, and the message is elsewhere.

symbols.name: LeaseExtender
symbols.doc:
LeaseExtender is the public alias for the capability of renewing a lease a
handler is still working under. Every broker here implements it.

symbols.name: MaxDeadlineOffset
symbols.doc:
MaxDeadlineOffset is the ceiling on [Policy].VisibilityTimeout and
[Policy].RetryDelay: a century, refused above it rather than clamped,
because a deadline past 2262 cannot be written into the durable broker's
file names and read back.

symbols.name: MaxSQLTableLen
symbols.doc:
MaxSQLTableLen is the longest table name [NewSQL] and [SQLMigration] accept,
in bytes: PostgreSQL's identifier limit.

symbols.name: MemoryConfig
symbols.doc: MemoryConfig is the public alias for [NewMemory]'s configuration.

symbols.name: Message
symbols.doc: Message is the public alias for one unit of work as the broker minted it.

symbols.name: MessageTooLarge

code.public: The message payload exceeds the queue's configured maximum size

symbols.doc:
MessageTooLarge refuses a payload above the policy's bound, at the
producer, where it can still be made smaller.

symbols.name: Nack
symbols.doc:
Nack is the public alias for what [Broker].Nack decided: retried, or
dead-lettered.

symbols.name: NewFile
symbols.doc:
NewFile returns the durable broker: its whole state is the directory in
cfg.Dir, so it survives the process that published into it and two brokers
over one directory are one queue.

It refuses at construction — never at first use — a policy it cannot
honour, a directory it cannot use safely, and a platform with no atomic
replace or no flushable directory handle. Windows is such a platform: after
the directory checks — which read its access control lists there — NewFile
returns the SDK's UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM, matched with
errors.Is(err, proc.UnsupportedPlatform).

The broker holds two directory descriptors and additionally implements
io.Closer, which releases them — reached by type assertion, as the session
file store's is, so Broker grows no method:

	if closer, ok := broker.(io.Closer); ok { defer closer.Close() }

The messages stay on disk; every call after Close fails.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.doc:
NewMemory returns the in-process test double: the port's full semantics,
no directory, no flush, and nothing that survives the process.

It refuses the same policies [NewFile] refuses, through the same guard,
which is what makes it an honest double.

symbols.name: NewSQL
symbols.doc:
NewSQL returns a durable broker whose queue is one table of the caller's
database, created by [SQLMigration]. Every call runs on the transaction its
context carries for cfg.Transactor, so a message published inside that
transaction exists if and only if it commits. It sends no statement.

It refuses at construction — never at first use — a policy it cannot honour
and a transactor, dialect or table it cannot use ([SQLQueueMisconfigured]).
The transactor must be the SDK's, or another core/data/sql Joiner and Deferrer.

symbols.name: NotRetryable

code.public: The message cannot be processed and was dead-lettered without a retry

symbols.doc:
NotRetryable is the failure no retry can fix: what a dead letter
records when [DoNotRetry] marked an error with no public words of its
own, or none at all.

symbols.name: Policy
symbols.doc: Policy is the public alias for the delivery discipline a broker enforces.

symbols.name: QueueBackendFailed

code.public: The queue's storage refused an operation

symbols.doc:
QueueBackendFailed reports a refusal from a durable broker's storage:
the filesystem's, or a statement the SQL broker's database did not
complete.

symbols.name: QueueDirectoryUnusable

code.public: The queue directory cannot be used safely

symbols.doc:
QueueDirectoryUnusable refuses a queue directory that is missing, is
not a directory, or is writable by accounts that must not be able to
inject or drain messages.

symbols.name: QueueMisconfigured

code.public: The queue policy is not one this broker can honour

symbols.doc: QueueMisconfigured refuses a Policy field the broker cannot honour.

symbols.name: Receipt
symbols.doc:
Receipt is the public alias for the opaque handle to one lease. Do not
parse it and do not construct one.

symbols.name: Rejecter
symbols.doc:
Rejecter is the public alias for the capability of dead-lettering a leased
message at once, with the cause that condemned it. Every broker here
implements it, and Consume uses it for a [DoNotRetry] failure.

symbols.name: SQLConfig
symbols.doc:
SQLConfig is the public alias for [NewSQL]'s configuration: Transactor,
Dialect and Table (required), Policy, and Clock.

symbols.name: SQLMigration
symbols.spelled: func(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
symbols.canonical: func(dialect github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Migration, error)
symbols.doc:
SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the one table an SQL queue
named table keeps on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version
table. Its Down drops the table, and every message in it. Its statement does
nothing when the table exists.

symbols.name: SQLQueueMisconfigured

code.public: The SQL queue's configuration cannot be used

symbols.doc:
SQLQueueMisconfigured refuses an SQLConfig no SQL broker could run: no
transactor, one it cannot join a transaction of, a dialect it cannot
spell, or a table name it cannot use.

symbols.name: UnknownReceipt

code.public: The receipt does not name a lease this queue issued

symbols.doc:
UnknownReceipt refuses an acknowledgement naming a lease this queue
never issued.

symbols.name: Wake
symbols.doc:
Wake is the public alias for what an idle consumer waits on: a signal the
next Publish or Nack in this process closes, and how long until something
the broker holds becomes receivable on its own.

symbols.name: Waker
symbols.doc:
Waker is the public alias for the capability of telling an idle consumer
when to look again. Every broker here implements it, and Consume uses it; a
broker of your own that omits it is simply polled.

symbols.name: Compare
symbols.doc:
Compare returns -1, 0 or +1 as v orders before, equal to or after w under
SemVer precedence. Build metadata is ignored, so v1.0.0+a and v1.0.0+b
compare equal. An invalid string orders below every version and equal to
every other invalid string.

symbols.name: IsPseudoVersion
symbols.doc:
IsPseudoVersion reports whether v is a Go pseudo-version, in any of its
three shapes, with or without build metadata. It recognises the shape: a
stamp whose digits are no real instant still makes one, and
[PseudoVersionTime] is what reports that the time does not read.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc:
IsValid reports whether v is a version: SemVer 2.0.0 with a leading "v",
or one of the shorthands "vMAJOR" and "vMAJOR.MINOR".

symbols.name: Prerelease
symbols.doc:
Prerelease returns the pre-release part of v with its leading hyphen —
"-rc.1" for "v1.0.0-rc.1+build" — or "" when v has none: a release, a
shorthand, or a string that is not a version, which [IsValid] tells apart.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionRev
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionRev returns the revision a pseudo-version names — by the
toolchain's convention a commit's first twelve hexadecimal digits — and
reports whether v is a pseudo-version at all.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionTime
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionTime returns the commit time a pseudo-version carries, in UTC
and to the second, and reports whether it could be read: false when v is
not a pseudo-version, or when its fourteen digits are no real instant.

symbols.name: Aborter
symbols.doc:
Aborter is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Transactor] that
holds a function until the work a context carries is undone — its
savepoint or its transaction rolled back — and drops it with a commit: the
complement of [Deferrer]. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: BeginFailed

code.public: The database refused to open a transaction

symbols.doc: BeginFailed reports a transaction the driver would not open.

symbols.name: Checker
symbols.doc: Checker is the public alias for the bounded liveness probe.

symbols.name: CommitFailed

code.public: The transaction could not be committed and had no effect

symbols.doc: CommitFailed reports a transaction that had NO effect.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the parameters every port is built from.

symbols.name: ConfigInvalid

code.public: The SQL configuration is incomplete and was refused

symbols.doc:
ConfigInvalid is returned by every constructor for a Config that could
never produce a working port.

symbols.name: Deferrer
symbols.doc:
Deferrer is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Transactor] that
holds a function until the transaction a context carries has committed, and
drops it with a rollback. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: Dialect
symbols.doc:
Dialect is the public alias for the closed set of SQL engines this SDK can
spell. For SQL you write yourself, it spells the engine's vocabulary — the
tokens the SDK's own statements are spelled with, never a statement:
[Dialect].Placeholder renders a bind marker ($1 on PostgreSQL, ? on MySQL and
SQLite), [Dialect].QuoteIdent a delimited name, its delimiter doubled
inside, and [Dialect].ForUpdate and [Dialect].ForUpdateSkipLocked a row-lock
clause, which SQLite — whose exclusion is its one write lock — renders as
nothing. QuoteIdent validates nothing: check a name before you interpolate
it. An unset Dialect renders no marker and no name, so a statement built
from it fails rather than passing for another engine's.

symbols.name: DialectMySQL
symbols.doc: DialectMySQL is MySQL 5.7+ / MariaDB 10.x with InnoDB.

symbols.name: DialectPostgres
symbols.doc: DialectPostgres is PostgreSQL 9.1+.

symbols.name: DialectRefused

code.public: That SQL engine is recognised and deliberately not supported

symbols.doc:
DialectRefused is returned by ParseDialect for an engine this SDK
recognises and declines. The reason travels in a field.

symbols.name: DialectSQLite
symbols.doc:
DialectSQLite is SQLite 3.6.8+. It has no advisory lock, so [NewMigrator]
serialises a run on the database file's write lock instead (ADR 0140).

symbols.name: DuplicateMigration

code.public: Two migrations declare the same version

symbols.doc: DuplicateMigration refuses two migrations declaring the same version.

symbols.name: Executor
symbols.doc:
Executor is the public alias for the read/write surface a statement runs
against. *sql.DB, *sql.Tx and *sql.Conn all satisfy it with no adapter, and
it deliberately carries no Commit, Rollback or Begin.

symbols.name: HealthCheckFailed

code.public: The database is not reachable

symbols.doc:
HealthCheckFailed reports a database that answered the probe with an
error.

symbols.name: HealthCheckTimeout

code.public: The database did not answer the health check in time

symbols.doc: HealthCheckTimeout reports a database that did not answer in time.

symbols.name: InvalidMigration

code.public: The migration is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidMigration is returned for a migration with version 0, an empty
name, a nil Up or a nil Down.

symbols.name: Irreversible
symbols.doc:
Irreversible is the [Step] a migration assigns to Down to declare, out loud,
that it cannot be reversed.

symbols.name: Joiner
symbols.doc:
Joiner is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Transactor] that
says where a statement issued under a context runs: in the transaction the
context carries, or on the pool. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: MigrateConfig
symbols.doc: MigrateConfig is the public alias for the migration runner's parameters.

symbols.name: Migration
symbols.doc:
Migration is the public alias for one versioned schema change and its
reversal.

symbols.name: MigrationFailed

code.public: A migration did not apply and was rolled back

symbols.doc:
MigrationFailed reports a migration that did not apply; it was rolled
back.

symbols.name: MigrationIrreversible

code.public: That migration was declared irreversible and cannot be rolled back

symbols.doc: MigrationIrreversible is what the Irreversible step returns.

symbols.name: MigrationLockTimeout

code.public: Another process is running migrations and did not finish in time

symbols.doc:
MigrationLockTimeout reports another process holding the migration lock
for the whole budget. Nothing was applied.

symbols.name: MigrationLockUnsupported

code.public: That dialect has no advisory lock, so migrations cannot be serialised

symbols.doc:
MigrationLockUnsupported refuses a Migrator on a dialect with no lock
that dies with its holder. No dialect this SDK speaks answers it since
SQLite's runner serialises on its file's write lock (ADR 0140).

symbols.name: MigrationOutOfOrder

code.public: A pending migration is older than one already applied

symbols.doc:
MigrationOutOfOrder refuses a pending migration older than one already
applied.

symbols.name: MigrationUnknownVersion

code.public: The database records a migration this build does not carry

symbols.doc:
MigrationUnknownVersion refuses a Down over a version this build does
not carry.

symbols.name: Migrator
symbols.doc: Migrator is the public alias for the schema-migration runner.

symbols.name: NestedIsolation

code.public: A nested transaction cannot change isolation or read-only mode

symbols.doc:
NestedIsolation is returned when a nested Transact asks for isolation
or read-only mode a savepoint cannot provide.

symbols.name: NewChecker
symbols.doc: NewChecker returns a liveness probe bounded by cfg.CheckTimeout.

symbols.name: NewMigrator
symbols.spelled: func(cfg Config, mig MigrateConfig) (runner Migrator, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewMigrator returns the migration runner. Every migration execution is
serialised: on the session's advisory lock where the engine has one
(PostgreSQL, MySQL), and on the database file's write lock on SQLite,
which has none (ADR 0140). No dialect the SDK speaks is refused for the
lock.

symbols.name: NewTransactor
symbols.doc:
NewTransactor returns the transaction manager for cfg.DB, applying
cfg.Pool to it.

symbols.name: ParseDialect
symbols.doc:
ParseDialect resolves a dialect name and never guesses. A recognised but
unsupported engine returns [DialectRefused] carrying why; an unrecognised
one returns [UnknownDialect].

symbols.name: PoolConfig
symbols.doc: PoolConfig is the public alias for the connection-pool policy.

symbols.name: PoolMisconfigured

code.public: The connection-pool policy is not one this SDK will apply

symbols.doc:
PoolMisconfigured refuses a pool policy whose zero value database/sql
would read as a decision nobody made — a non-positive MaxOpen.

symbols.name: Preparer
symbols.doc:
Preparer is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Executor]: an
executor that can also prepare a statement. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: RollbackFailed

code.public: Rolling the transaction back did not complete cleanly

symbols.doc: RollbackFailed travels alongside the error that triggered the rollback.

symbols.name: SavepointFailed

code.public: A savepoint statement was rejected by the database

symbols.doc:
SavepointFailed reports a rejected savepoint statement; the "statement"
field names which of the three.

symbols.name: Statements
symbols.doc:
Statements returns a [Step] that runs the given statements in order on the
transaction's executor.

It is the smallest useful helper and deliberately not a file loader: it
invents no directory layout, no naming convention and no parser. Where the
text comes from — a literal, an embed.FS, a generator — stays yours.

symbols.name: Step
symbols.doc: Step is the public alias for one direction of a migration.

symbols.name: Transact
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, tm Transactor, fn TxFunc) error
symbols.doc:
Transact runs fn inside a transaction with the driver's default isolation.

It is the ergonomic form of [Transactor].Transact for the common case. The
port itself keeps the options parameter so it never needs a second method
(ADR 0039); this helper keeps the call site short.

symbols.name: Transactor
symbols.doc: Transactor is the public alias for the transaction manager.

symbols.name: TxClosed

code.public: That transaction handle is no longer valid

symbols.doc:
TxClosed reports an Executor used after the scope that lent it
returned.

symbols.name: TxFunc
symbols.doc: TxFunc is the public alias for a unit of work run inside a transaction.

symbols.name: TxOptions
symbols.doc:
TxOptions is the public alias for one transaction's isolation and
read-only-ness. The zero value defers to the driver.

symbols.name: TxPoisoned

code.public: The transaction is no longer usable and will not be committed

symbols.doc:
TxPoisoned refuses every operation on a transaction whose savepoint
rollback failed. It is never committed.

symbols.name: UnknownDialect

code.public: The SQL dialect is not one this SDK supports

symbols.doc:
UnknownDialect is returned by ParseDialect for a name this SDK has
never heard of.

symbols.name: VersionTableInvalid

code.public: The version-table name is not a plain SQL identifier

symbols.doc:
VersionTableInvalid refuses a version-table name that is not a plain
SQL identifier.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the name a Compressor registers under. The zero value is
reserved as invalid.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc: Available returns the registered Algorithms, sorted.

symbols.name: BoundedDecompressor
symbols.doc:
BoundedDecompressor is the optional extension of a Compressor that can be
told how much plaintext it may produce; DecompressBounded uses it when the
scheme has it.

symbols.name: CodeCompressedFrameInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeCompressedFrameInvalid identifies a malformed compressed frame of the
codec package, or a frame its decompression-bomb guard refused (0.2.5.4).

symbols.name: CodeDecompressedTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeDecompressedTooLarge identifies a stream whose plaintext would exceed
the ceiling its caller gave (0.2.5.6).

symbols.name: CodeFlateFailed
symbols.doc: CodeFlateFailed identifies a stream compress/flate refused (0.3.26.2).

symbols.name: CodeGzipFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeGzipFailed identifies a stream compress/gzip refused, compressing or
decompressing (0.3.26.1).

symbols.name: CodeUnknownCompressor
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownCompressor identifies an Algorithm no imported package has
registered (0.2.5.1).

symbols.name: CodeZlibFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeZlibFailed identifies a stream compress/zlib refused (0.3.26.3): the
RFC 1950 envelope, told apart from raw DEFLATE because a stream one of
them refuses is often valid under the other.

symbols.name: Compress
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte) (encoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Compress compresses src with the scheme registered under algo and appends
the result to dst. An unregistered algo is refused with UnknownCompressor
and dst comes back as it was.

symbols.name: CompressedFrameInvalid

code.public: Compressed frame is malformed or exceeds the safety bound

symbols.doc: CompressedFrameInvalid is the sentinel of [CodeCompressedFrameInvalid].

symbols.name: Compressor
symbols.doc:
Compressor is one compression scheme: Compress and Decompress append to dst.
Implementations are safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: Decompress
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Decompress decompresses src with the scheme registered under algo and
appends the result to dst, bounded by the scheme's own backstop. To bound
it by a number of your own, call DecompressBounded. An unregistered algo is
refused with UnknownCompressor and dst comes back as it was.

symbols.name: DecompressBounded
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte, limit int64) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(algo github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/transform.Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte, limit int64) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
DecompressBounded decompresses src with the scheme registered under algo
and appends the result to dst, producing at most limit bytes of plaintext:
a stream that would produce more is refused with DecompressedTooLarge and
dst comes back as it was. A limit of zero admits an empty stream and nothing
else, and a negative limit is read as zero rather than given a meaning of
its own.

A scheme implementing BoundedDecompressor stops at limit, so the work is
bounded too. A scheme that does not — a consumer's own, or one of the
third-party module's — is decompressed under its own backstop and judged
afterwards: declining to tighten the work can never change the verdict,
only the bytes touched reaching it.

symbols.name: DecompressedTooLarge

code.public: Decompressed payload exceeds the caller's ceiling

symbols.doc:
DecompressedTooLarge is the sentinel of [CodeDecompressedTooLarge],
returned as is.

symbols.name: Flate
symbols.doc: Flate is the raw DEFLATE stream of RFC 1951, with no envelope.

symbols.name: FlateFailed

code.public: flate transform failed

symbols.doc: FlateFailed is the sentinel of [CodeFlateFailed].

symbols.name: Gzip
symbols.doc: Gzip is RFC 1952: a DEFLATE stream in a gzip envelope with a CRC-32.

symbols.name: GzipFailed

code.public: gzip transform failed

symbols.doc:
GzipFailed is the sentinel of [CodeGzipFailed]; the stdlib's error is
kept beneath it.

symbols.name: Lookup
symbols.doc: Lookup returns the Compressor registered under algo.

symbols.name: UnknownCompressor

code.public: No compressor is registered under that algorithm

symbols.doc:
UnknownCompressor is the sentinel of [CodeUnknownCompressor], returned
as is.

symbols.name: Zlib
symbols.doc:
Zlib is the RFC 1950 envelope with an Adler-32 — what HTTP calls
"deflate".

symbols.name: ZlibFailed

code.public: zlib transform failed

symbols.doc: ZlibFailed is the sentinel of [CodeZlibFailed].

symbols.name: AtomicWriter
symbols.doc:
AtomicWriter is the public alias for the publication capability, reached by
type assertion on a filesystem this package did not build.

symbols.name: DirectoryNotEmpty

code.public: That directory still has entries in it

symbols.doc:
DirectoryNotEmpty is returned by Remove for a directory that still has
entries. RemoveAll is the recursive call.

symbols.name: DirectorySyncFailed

code.public: The file was published but the directory entry was not flushed

symbols.doc:
DirectorySyncFailed is returned when the rename succeeded and the
directory entry could not be flushed. The content IS published; only
its survival across a power loss is in doubt, and it is deliberately
not rolled back.

symbols.name: FS
symbols.doc:
FS is the public alias for the read half, which is io/fs.FS unchanged. It
exists so a signature can say "an SDK filesystem" without implying that
anything about reading is different here.

symbols.name: FullFS
symbols.doc:
FullFS is the public alias for the union both constructors return: a
[WritableFS] that is also an [AtomicWriter]. A parameter should still ask
for the narrowest thing it uses.

symbols.name: InvalidPath

code.public: That path is not usable on this filesystem

symbols.doc:
InvalidPath is returned for a name outside the fs.ValidPath grammar —
rooted, empty, or carrying a "." or ".." element — and for the root
itself on any call that writes or removes.

symbols.name: InvalidPermission

code.public: A file mode is required and must be a plain permission mode

symbols.doc:
InvalidPermission is returned for a zero file mode, which is never read
as "pick a default", and for any mode carrying setuid, setgid, sticky
or a type bit.

symbols.name: NewMem
symbols.doc:
NewMem returns an empty in-memory filesystem containing only its root.

It takes no arguments on purpose: every knob it could offer would be one a
consumer's test has to set before it can assert anything, and the value of
this type is that a filesystem double costs one line.

symbols.name: NewOS
symbols.doc:
NewOS opens root as a filesystem confined to that directory tree.

It returns proc.UnsupportedPlatform on a GOOS that lacks the mechanics this
filesystem's guarantees rest on, and [RootUnavailable] when the directory
cannot be opened. Both are construction-time refusals, so a misconfiguration
is reported where the program is wired rather than on the first write.

The filesystem holds the directory's descriptor and additionally implements
io.Closer, which releases it; every call after Close fails.

symbols.name: NotRegularFile

code.public: That path already holds something other than a file

symbols.doc:
NotRegularFile is returned when the name — or a component of it —
exists and is not the kind of thing the call needs it to be.

symbols.name: PathEscaped

code.public: That path leaves the filesystem it was resolved against

symbols.doc:
PathEscaped is returned when a name resolved outside the filesystem's
root, and when a write's final component is a symbolic link.

symbols.name: PublishFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not publish that file

symbols.doc:
PublishFailed is returned when an atomic publication did not complete.
The previous content is intact and no temporary survives, so the
operation is safe to retry and safe to abandon.

symbols.name: ReadFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not read that path

symbols.doc:
ReadFailed is returned when an open, stat or listing was refused. The
cause stays in the chain, so errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) still
answers.

symbols.name: RootUnavailable

code.public: The filesystem root could not be opened

symbols.doc:
RootUnavailable is returned by NewOS when the root cannot be opened:
absent, not a directory, or not searchable by this process.

symbols.name: WritableFS
symbols.doc:
WritableFS is the public alias for the write half: the four write verbs on
top of the embedded [FS]. It is frozen — a new capability arrives as a
sibling interface, never as a fifth method.

symbols.name: WriteFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not write that path

symbols.doc:
WriteFailed is returned when a create, write, mkdir or remove was
refused, and keeps its cause the same way.
